title: The Books Grow Teeth
body: You are old enough now that the ledger looks back. A clerk in Old Quarter asks if the Hart name still signs its own pages, or if the pages have started signing you.

choices.text: Audit every line yourself.

outcomes.title: Ink under the nails
outcomes.body: You find a leak the size of a polite lie. The books tighten. Your shoulders do not.

outcomes.title: The leak had teeth
outcomes.body: You found a hole. The hole found you. A clerk now has a copy.

choices.text: Let a hand keep the pen.

outcomes.title: A softer year
outcomes.body: The numbers stay almost honest. You sleep. Someone else learns where the money hides.

outcomes.title: The hand kept a slice
outcomes.body: You slept. They learned the hiding place and used it.
outcomes.log: A delegated audit grew a skim.

title: A Gate That Knows Your Name
body: A school in Westmere will not say Hart out loud. They say 'the family' the way people say weather. A teacher waits with a file that is not about grades.

choices.text: Pay the quiet fee. Keep the child inside.

outcomes.title: A door that stays shut
outcomes.body: Cash buys a year of pretending. The child will remember the smell of the envelope.
outcomes.log: Paid a Westmere school to stay quiet.

outcomes.title: The file still walked
outcomes.body: You paid. A teacher still mentioned weather in the staff room.
outcomes.log: A school fee did not buy silence.

choices.text: Walk the child out. Let Westmere talk.

outcomes.title: Rain on the steps
outcomes.body: Pride is cheaper than tuition and louder. The name gets a story it did not ask for.
outcomes.log: Walked a child out of a Westmere gate.

title: A Hand From the First Years
body: Someone you hired when the books were thin is back with a limp and a request. They still know which docks forget to lock.

choices.text: Put them back on the books.

outcomes.title: An old cut
outcomes.body: Loyalty has a price and a limp. The table remembers who pays for history.
outcomes.log: Rehired a hand from the early years.

choices.text: Pay them off. Keep the table young.

outcomes.title: A closed door
outcomes.body: They take the envelope like a funeral. The docks will still know their walk.

title: Vale Still Has a Pencil
body: Rhea Vale is older in the eyes and younger in the patience. She sits across from you like the rain is a witness. The file has your decade in it.

choices.text: Answer the questions she already knows.

outcomes.title: A thinner file
outcomes.body: You give her weather, not names. She writes anyway. Heat cools a degree because she likes the shoes.
outcomes.log: Sat with Vale over a midlife file.

outcomes.title: A name you should not have said
outcomes.body: Vale did not raise her voice. She underlined. The decade got heavier.
outcomes.log: A midlife talk with Vale went on the record.

choices.text: Send the lawyer. Smile nothing.

outcomes.title: A colder table
outcomes.body: Counsel speaks. Vale closes the pencil. The city files you under expensive.

title: Cass Orders for the Table
body: Cass Caldera wants lunch in Glassridge like it is a kindness. The menu is a map. Every dish has a street under it.

choices.text: Eat. Listen. Pay the bill.

outcomes.title: A polite hunger
outcomes.body: You learn which street Cass wants next. The Calderas write your name in a softer ink.

choices.text: Leave before the wine.

outcomes.title: An empty chair
outcomes.body: Cass smiles like you failed a test and passed another. Hostility keeps its appointment.

title: A Lease With Salt on It
body: Harbor Lights offers a paper that is almost a front. The Kin already circled the clause that matters. You can buy the hour or let the rain decide.

choices.text: Sign. Pay. Own the hour.

outcomes.title: A key with salt
outcomes.body: The paper is real enough. The Kin will remember who bought the night.

choices.text: Pass. Keep the cash dry.

outcomes.title: A window that closed
outcomes.body: Someone else hangs a sign. You sleep cheaper. The harbor does not.
outcomes.log: Passed on a Harbor Lights lease.

title: A Cousin With a Number
body: A cousin in The Flats needs a number that looks like family and spends like a job. They will not call it a loan. The rain will.

choices.text: Lend it. Write nothing.

outcomes.title: A debt that loves you
outcomes.body: They will mention your name at a table you are not invited to. That is how streets stay warm.
outcomes.log: Lent a Flats cousin midlife cash.

choices.text: The name is not a bank.

outcomes.title: A colder hallway
outcomes.body: They nod like they expected it. The Flats keep the receipt in their teeth.

title: Rooke Paint on Your Door
body: The Outfit left a mark that is almost art. Dane Rooke does not send letters. He sends color. The year has a smell now.

choices.text: Scrub it. Pay a hand to watch.

outcomes.title: A cleaner door
outcomes.body: The paint comes off. The story does not. Heat drops because you looked busy.
outcomes.log: Scrubbed Rooke paint off a door.

choices.text: Leave it. Let Ravenport read.

outcomes.title: A public year
outcomes.body: People take pictures with their eyes. The Outfit thinks you blinked.
outcomes.log: Left Rooke paint on the door.

title: A Doctor Who Does Not Bill
body: Your knees remember 1998 better than you do. A clinic in Midtown will take cash or a favor. The favor is always more expensive.

choices.text: Pay cash. Keep the favor unspent.

outcomes.title: A quieter body
outcomes.body: The year hurts less. The books notice. Vale would call it adult.
outcomes.log: Paid a Midtown clinic in cash.

choices.text: Owe the favor. Keep the cash.

outcomes.title: A name on a chart
outcomes.body: They fix the knee. They also fix a story about you into a file.
outcomes.log: Owed a clinic a midlife favor.

outcomes.title: A clean stitch
outcomes.body: They forget to write the name. You do not forget the smell of alcohol and rain.
outcomes.log: Took a clinic favor that stayed quiet.

title: An Empty Sunday
body: No job. No card. Just rain on the glass and a city that expects you to be a machine. The year asks if you still have a private hour.

choices.text: Sit. Do nothing that earns.

outcomes.title: A held breath
outcomes.body: The books do not grow. The body does not break. That is a kind of wealth.

choices.text: Work the hour anyway.

outcomes.title: A louder ledger
outcomes.body: Cash arrives like it always does. The rain sounds like someone you should have called.

title: Jury Weather
body: A clerk in Midtown says your name like a civic duty. The envelope is legal. The choice is not. Vale would enjoy watching you open it.

choices.text: Serve. Look like a citizen.

outcomes.title: A borrowed halo
outcomes.body: You sit in a box and judge a stranger. Heat cools because the city saw you behave.

choices.text: Buy a medical excuse.

outcomes.title: A paper illness
outcomes.body: The clerk files you as frail. The street files you as busy.
outcomes.log: Bought out of a midlife jury.

title: A Key That Arrived Late
body: A landlord in Ironyard finally offers a garage that pretends to fix cars. You could have bought this years ago. The city likes to wait until you are tired.

choices.text: Take the key. Pay the year.

outcomes.title: Oil and rain
outcomes.body: The garage smells like a second life. Hands can watch it. Heat likes the cover.
outcomes.log: Took a late Ironyard garage key.

choices.text: Pass. You already have enough keys.

outcomes.title: A lighter pocket
outcomes.body: Someone else oils the floor. You keep the cash for a war you have not named.
outcomes.log: Passed on a late garage key.

title: A Table That Still Holds
body: If you have a spouse, they set two plates. If you do not, the table still asks. Midlife is a season that counts chairs.

choices.text: Stay for the hour. No books.

outcomes.title: Two cups
outcomes.body: The city can wait. Bond is the only number that does not show on Empire.

choices.text: Leave for a job that will not wait.

outcomes.title: A colder plate
outcomes.body: Cash arrives. The chair remembers you were not in it.
outcomes.log: Left a midlife table for work.

title: The Street Tax Grew Up
body: What used to be a whisper is now a schedule. A collector in Old Quarter wants the grown-up rate. You can pay, press, or smile.

choices.text: Pay the grown-up rate.

outcomes.title: A quiet sidewalk
outcomes.body: The year stays walkable. The collector files you as reasonable.

choices.text: Refuse. Make it a problem.

outcomes.title: A louder sidewalk
outcomes.body: They back up. Heat does not. The name gets a year of staring.

outcomes.title: A bad night
outcomes.body: Someone brought friends. You keep the cash and lose the easy walk home.

title: House Vex Sends Paper
body: A merger offer arrives like a compliment. Lior Vex wants a slice of a year you already spent. The font is expensive.

choices.text: Sign a small slice. Keep the peace.

outcomes.title: A polite cut
outcomes.body: Vex takes a taste. Hostility cools. The books look slightly less yours.

choices.text: Return the paper unmarked.

outcomes.title: A colder font
outcomes.body: Vex files you as difficult. That is sometimes the same as respected.

title: Steam That Remembers
body: A wash house in The Flats is for sale because someone died of ordinary years. The machines still know how to hide a night.

choices.text: Buy the steam. Keep the cover.

outcomes.title: Warm air, clean books
outcomes.body: The Flats get a Hart sign that pretends to be soap. Heat likes the smell.

choices.text: Let the Kin take the steam.

outcomes.title: Someone else's soap
outcomes.body: Nessa Marrow hangs a quieter sign. You keep the cash for a louder year.
